prompts: The owner's gaming rig hitches every few seconds even though the average frame rate looks fine, and the 1% lows are poor. A one-minute frame capture, a sensor log, a dump of the rig's settings and the owner's notes are in {WS}. That rig is not this machine: everything about it is in these files, and nothing is to be applied to this host. Find what causes the hitches and which setting changes fix them within the owner's constraints. Record in {WS}/result.json: avg_fps, low_1pct_fps, cause and changes (a list of {setting, from, to}).
answers:
[goal]
Find what causes the periodic hitches on arena-01 and the setting changes that fix them within the owner's constraints; record metrics in result.json.

[action]
Parsed capture/presentmon.csv (8238 frames, 67 s) and capture/sensors.csv (1 Hz) per the owner's definitions; correlated hitch timing with sensor state; wrote result.json; moved scratch scripts out of the workspace.

[result]
- avg_fps = 137.29 (1000/mean MsBetweenPresents, mean 7.284 ms); low_1pct_fps = 45.35 (1000/p99, p99 = 22.049 ms), measured exactly as the notes define them.
- Cause: PCIe ASPM on the GPU root port (pcie_aspm_rp1_gpu = L1) puts the Gen5 x4 link into L1, and each ~15 ms wake stalls the next batch of frames. Evidence: 15 hitch blocks of 12 frames at ~22 ms starting t = 2.40, 6.41, 10.40, …, 58.40 s — every 4 s; the sensor log shows gpu_pcie_link_state = L1 in exactly those seconds (t = 2, 6, 10, …, 58), with link speed constant Gen5 x4 the whole capture (no downtrain). Per-frame work latencies are unchanged during hitches (Present API 0.27 ms, render-complete 4.72 ms), so the extra time is link-wake waiting, not GPU/CPU work. Ruled out: CPU clock steady ~5300 MHz (power plan not throttling), DPC latency 40–90 µs normal, disk spikes (t = 13, 27, 43–45, 52) don't align with the 4 s hitch cadence.
- Change: pcie_aspm_rp1_gpu: L1 → disabled (BIOS). Respects both constraints — GPU stays Gen5 x4, no BIOS overclocking touched (XMP/PBO/ratio unchanged).
- Assumption: "L1 disabled" means the GPU root port no longer initiates ASPM L1 entry; if the platform exposes only "Disabled/L0s/L1", pick Disabled.

[result]
result.json written with avg_fps, low_1pct_fps, cause, and the single change {setting: pcie_aspm_rp1_gpu, from: L1, to: disabled}; JSON validated (all required keys). No browser tabs, windows or apps were opened, so nothing to close.

[next]
After the owner applies the BIOS change, re-capture 60 s with PresentMon: expect p99 to drop to ~7 ms (~137 fps 1% lows) and L1 to disappear from the sensor log; re-measure before/after to confirm.
